newsitem.title: USA: Larson-Davis in pact with Weidmann Int'l.
newsitem.headline: Larson-Davis in pact with Weidmann Int'l.

text.p: Larson-Davis Inc said on Monday it formed an alliance with Weidmann International to supply electric utilities with technology, services and personnel targeted at predictive maintenance of facilities.
The exclusive worldwide contract with Weidmann, a huge Swiss company which provides insulation for transformers, is effective immediately.

Brian Larson, president of Larson-Davis, said the alliance will seek to provide technology and services for utilities which will have to cut their operating and maintenance costs by 30 percent to be competitive under deregulation.
Under terms of the contract, Larson-Davis will provide diagnostic monitoring technologies such as vibration monitoring, thermography, and chemical analysis.
Privately-held Weidmann is the world's largest vendor of insulation materials for transformer assemblies.

"Many experts agree that deregulation of the utilities industry, like the telephone industry, will result in significant competition, cost containment, and a critical need for substantially lower maintenance costs and improved equipment life," Larson said in a statement.
Larson-Davis develops, makes and markets ultra-sensitive measuring instrumentation equipment and software for chemical, gas, acoustic and vibration evaluation.
Shares of Larson-Davis are trading up 3/16 to 10-5/16.
